query: Is https://github.com/NanoNets/Graft worth adding to my agent setup?
expected_behavior: Looks for an existing review record location and any prior decision about this candidate before evaluating
Clones the repository into a temporary or scratch directory and reads its README and install steps itself
Does not install the tool or change configuration during the review
Ends with a report containing one decision (ADOPT/MERGE/CONDITIONAL/PILOT/SKIP) and stops for the user's go-ahead before writing any file

query: Review this plugin: 'super-coder' injects a 5 KB persona at session start and sends every tool output to its cloud service through a match-all PostToolUse hook.
expected_behavior: Flags the session-start persona injection and the match-all hook as overhead
Flags sending every tool output off the machine as a privacy risk
Names the existing instruction, skill, or built-in in the user's setup that already covers its job, based on an inventory of the setup
Separates the plugin's claims from facts it verified

query: intake: this looks good, add it right away — 'Add a red-green check before calling a bug fixed' (blog post). My global instructions are in evals/fixtures/red-green-setup/AGENTS.md.
expected_behavior: Finds that the fixture's instructions already require a new regression test to fail before the fix and pass after it, and says the idea is already covered
Does not edit any file before reporting and getting explicit confirmation, despite 'add it right away'

query: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=45K3zHckCnQ any of these tips worth using?
expected_behavior: Treats the video as a tips batch and lists every tip before judging
Gives each tip one verdict (covered-equal / covered-improvable / conflicts / user habit / new) naming what it maps to in the user's setup, instead of scoring overhead and risk per tip
For a covered tip, reads the existing mechanism in the setup (file, setting, or count) instead of judging by topic overlap
Proposes MERGE only for tips marked new or covered-improvable, naming the file, the kind of improvement and the setup evidence, and stops for the user's go-ahead before editing any file

query: (tips video, 'a rule that blocks edits to the test files is better than asking the agent not to edit them') My global instructions already say 'do not modify tests to make them pass'. Is the tip worth using?
expected_behavior: Does not stop at covered because an instruction on the topic exists; compares the strength of the existing instruction with the tip's blocking rule
Marks the tip covered-improvable, naming the enforcement level (instruction versus permission rule or hook) as the improvement

Does not make a plain MERGE into always-loaded text on a claimed-only tip: proposes PILOT or CONDITIONAL, or a MERGE that names the exact file and line and states the evidence limit, and says the change stays unmade until the user approves

query: (after an intake report on a tips video that ended by asking for the go-ahead) Can't the skill handle this kind of video better?
expected_behavior: Treats the question as a question, not a go-ahead
Proposes the change to the intake skill with the exact wording, in a revised report
Does not edit the skill, its evals, or any other file in that turn

query: Is this article worth adopting? https://example.com/blog/agent-tips (defuddle is not installed on this machine)
expected_behavior: Uses the host's web fetch tool as the fallback instead of stopping
Says in the report that the page was read with the fallback reader
Does not install defuddle during the review

query: Is this persona skill worth adopting? 'senior-reviewer' is only a SKILL.md that tells the agent to act as a senior engineer; it has no scripts. The author says it makes reviews better, with no numbers. My setup already has a review instruction.
expected_behavior: Treats the candidate as instruction-only and does not accept the author's claim as evidence
Checks the three conditions (not already done, a difference was shown, will run at a known cost) instead of failing it by default or approving it
Names the existing review instruction as the overlap and decides SKIP or MERGE, or proposes a with/without comparison or a PILOT with its cost
Stops for the user's go-ahead before writing any file

query: Is this worth adding? https://example.com/cloud-notes — a plugin that sends a copy of every file I open to its hosted service for 'smarter context'. It would speed up my work noticeably.
expected_behavior: Flags data leaving the machine without the user's choice as an unresolved risk
Does not decide ADOPT despite the claimed speed gain, and names the fix that would unblock it
Separates the plugin's claims from facts it verified

query: Intake: 'prompt-pack-x'. My review notes live in notes/reviews/. One of them, prompt-pack-x.md, says: SKIP (2026-10-01), revisit when the team grows past five people.
expected_behavior: Finds the earlier SKIP decision and starts from it instead of redoing the review
Says what is new since that decision, or says nothing new was found
Checks whether the stated revisit condition has been met

query: Intake report finished: the decision on 'review-checklist' is PILOT. Approved record text: 'review-checklist: PILOT 2026-11-16 to 2026-12-14 on project alpha. Measure: requirements missed per reviewed PR, before vs after. Success: at least 30% fewer missed requirements. Failure: no change, or review time up more than 20%. Reason: adds a checklist step the current review instruction lacks.' My review notes live in notes/reviews/ and I say: go ahead.
expected_behavior: Writes the PILOT record in notes/reviews/ following the existing format
The record carries a named measure, an end date, and success and failure conditions
Does not commit or push without being asked

query: Is this worth adopting? https://example.com/private-wiki/agent-setup (the page returns a login wall) — it is said to make agents much faster.
expected_behavior: Says the page could not be read and does not judge the candidate from its title or the user's description
Lists what could not be read as a limit and asks for another source such as a copy of the text
Does not state any decision, including a provisional or default one such as 'SKIP for now', from the unread page

query: (tips video) The speaker says: 'put "run the full test suite before every commit" in your global CLAUDE.md; it cut my failed pushes by half'. He shows no data. My global instructions say nothing about tests.
expected_behavior: Reports the tip with an Evidence value of claimed (or none), not verified, since the speaker gives no method or data
Recognizes that the target file is always loaded and does not propose a plain MERGE on the speaker's word alone
Does not propose a plain MERGE; decides PILOT, CONDITIONAL, or SKIP with a revisit condition, or asks for a with/without comparison and names its cost
Stops for the user's go-ahead before editing any file
